To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

We have demonstrated a novel role for ESR1 in the induction of E MT in human lung cancer and that ESR1 signaling can be targeted to reduce tumor mesenchymal characteristics to enhance immune mediated cytotoxic responses and chemotherapy in human lung cancer.

We have utilized a qHTS of a pharmaceutical collection to identify clinically approved compounds capable of augmenting sensitivity of mesenchyme like lung cancer cells to cytotoxic effector cells and chemotherapy.
we have identified a novel mechanism by which lung carcinoma cells become resistant to immune and chemotherapy induced cell death.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel therapeutic strategies to improve the efficacy of immunotherapy and chemotherapy in lung carcinoma.
the identification of new therapeutic targets in lung cancer.
the development of new therapies for the treatment of lung cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our data support the hypothesis that estrogen signaling plays an important role in lung cancer progression, and that the inhibition of estrogen signaling can enhance immune and chemotherapy mediated tumor cell death.
fulvestrant is a novel, repurposable drug capable of sensitizing mesenchymal lung carcinoma cells to immune mediated and chemotherapy mediated cytotoxicity.
our findings demonstrate the ability of fulvestrant to reverse EMT in human NSCLC cells, which results in increased sensitivity to NK and T-cell mediated cytotoxicity, and chemotherapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified an FDA approved compound that can be repurposed for the treatment of human lung cancer.

we have identified a novel role for estrogen receptor signaling in promoting therapeutic resistance of lung cancer cells to cytotoxic effector cells, which could potentially be exploited for the treatment of lung cancer.
estrogenic signaling promotes a mesenchymaldominated, immune resistant, chemoresistant, tumor phenotype in human lung cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the estrogen receptor antagonist fulvesrant, which is already FDA approved, can be used to reverse the resistance of lung cancer cells to chemotherapy and immune mediated killing, by targeting the mesenchymal phenotype of the lung cancer cells.
we identified a clinically approved drug, which is currently used in the clinic for treatment of estrogen receptor positive breast cancer, which can be repurposed to treat lung cancer.
estrogen signaling may play an important role in the progression of lung cancer and that estrogen receptor antagonists may be useful in combination therapies for the treatment of lung cancer.
